workflowPage.title: Workflows that separate decisions, controls and effects.
workflowPage.lead: Each automation is split by responsibility. Here are the largest workflows, why they exist and what still needs runtime validation.
workflowPage.truth: The screenshots come from a local n8n editor with the versioned JSON files. They show imported architecture, not production executions.

rfq.title: MA RFQ Multimodal Agents
rfq.summary: The main workflow receives text, PDFs and images and prepares a decision package before sales and engineering create an offer.
rfq.why: A technical RFQ mixes requirements, documents and internal knowledge. Handling it in one hidden prompt would conceal important steps.
rfq.purpose: Separate evidence extraction, critical review and readiness decisions while keeping final approval with a person.
rfq.how: The webhook normalises the input. Evidence Agent queries approved sources. Challenger finds contradictions. Deterministic rules calculate blockers and routing.
set: Evidence Agent with approved Markdown knowledge
rfq.state: The workflow is versioned and connected to the public demo. Credentials and company-specific rules stay outside the repository.
rfq.imageAlt: Multimodal RFQ workflow imported in the n8n editor

rag.title: Second Brain · Secure Ask
rag.summary: Second Brain uses two workflows. Capture prepares and indexes notes. Ask retrieves context, treats notes as untrusted data and validates the sources used.
rag.why: Capturing knowledge and answering questions have different risks and effects. Separating them exposes writes, retrieval and the trust boundary.
rag.purpose: Prevent a retrieved note from giving orders to the system and prevent decorative citations from being shown as real evidence.
rag.how: Ask validates identity and question, creates the embedding, retrieves owner-isolated matches, bounds the context and accepts only validated source IDs.
set: Capture: normalisation, chunking, embeddings and ingestion
Ask: search, bounded context, answer and citations
rag.state: Both JSON exports are versioned and inactive. The lab reproduces defences; end-to-end execution with real services still requires configuration.
rag.imageAlt: Second Brain Ask workflow imported in the n8n editor

fridge.title: Telegram Audio Intake v2
fridge.summary: The large workflow converts a Telegram voice note into a validated inventory event without letting a model choose identity, SQL or credentials.
fridge.why: A spoken instruction may be duplicated, incomplete or misheard. Applying it directly to inventory would be difficult to audit.
fridge.purpose: Keep the original message, deduplicate, transcribe, extract a structured proposal and request review when confidence is low.
fridge.how: It verifies Telegram, creates an ingestion record, transcribes, validates the event against a contract and only then prepares a deterministic Supabase change.
set: 01 Audio Intake v2: receipt, voice, validation and inventory
90 Error Handler: classification and safe notification
InventoryEvent contract shared with the application
fridge.state: Both workflows are versioned and importable. Telegram, transcription and Supabase need credentials and a controlled test before activation.
fridge.imageAlt: FridgeFlow audio workflow imported in the n8n editor

agent.title: 03 Orchestrator
agent.summary: Agent Observatory splits an autonomous loop into nine workflows so start, control, agents, commit, observation and errors have independent boundaries.
agent.why: One giant workflow would hide the kill switch, GitHub permissions and the decision to continue another round.
agent.purpose: Make visible which agent proposes, which one builds, when GitHub is changed and which external control can stop the next round.
agent.how: Orchestrator calls Explorer, Builder, Commit and Observer in sequence. Before every round it checks Control Gate and stores messages and events in Supabase.
set: Public Start, Control Gate and Orchestrator
Explorer, Builder, GitHub Commit and Observer
agent.state: Nine statically validated JSON files and a synthetic public trace. Combined execution in a production n8n runtime remains experimental.
agent.imageAlt: Agent Observatory Orchestrator workflow imported in the n8n editor

music.title: Music School Enquiry
music.summary: A small workflow receives a structured enquiry, validates the fields and prepares a short notification for the person managing the school.
music.why: A family needs to ask about a course and schedule without understanding internal planning or completing a long form.
music.purpose: Turn the enquiry into a clear Telegram message while leaving the reply and final confirmation with a person.
music.how: The webhook receives course, level, day and contact. A deterministic step validates the payload and the Telegram node notifies the configured administrator.
set: The final reply is always human
music.state: Importable, inactive template. The public demo only shows a preview and sends no data.

approachPage.title: The difference is in how the system is checked.
approachPage.lead: I build a surface that makes the flow understandable, separate decisions from effects and document what has not been validated yet.

evidence.title: Start with proof you can open
evidence.copy: The interface shows the path with synthetic data and lets people inspect the result without preparing private infrastructure.
evidence.detail: The demo is not the integration. It helps agree on behaviour, language and decisions before connecting real systems.
evidence.result: Something concrete to discuss from day one.

human.title: Human review is part of the design
human.copy: When a decision can affect a customer, inventory or repository, the workflow prepares evidence and keeps final control with a person.
human.detail: Models can extract or propose. Rules control routing, and sensitive effects need an explicit boundary.

boundaries.title: Working, simulated and experimental stay separate
boundaries.copy: Each case distinguishes implemented behaviour, demo data and architecture that still needs a real environment.
boundaries.detail: I do not present n8n imports as production runs or a Telegram preview as a real message.
boundaries.result: The technical state can be read without guessing.

delivery.title: Build, tests and documentation are the delivery
delivery.copy: Repositories include instructions, architecture, screenshots and reproducible checks before GitHub Pages publication.
delivery.detail: Credentials, customer documents and personal data stay out. Changes are checked on desktop and mobile and deployed from the repository.
delivery.result: A base another person can inspect and continue.

approachPage.closingTitle: A demo you can open and an architecture you can discuss.

rfq.name: Menz RFQ Copilot
rfq.summary: A fit check for complex technical requests before an offer is prepared.
rfq.problem: Sales and engineering receive requirements spread across forms, email and documents. Contradictions can surface late.
rfq.solution: Structures the request, separates evidence from questions, flags contradictions and prepares customer questions.
rfq.how: Text, PDFs and images pass through evidence, critical review and readiness rules before a human decision package is created.
rfq.try: Load the synthetic RFQ and inspect the decision, blockers, sources and reply draft.
rfq.working: Interface, multimodal analysis, deterministic rules, evidence and review agents, and provider rate-limit fallback.
rfq.simulated: The demo uses a synthetic RFQ and does not represent a real customer.
rfq.experimental: Company-specific rules and knowledge need configuration before production use.
rfq.tech: React, TypeScript, Vite, n8n, PDF and image analysis.
rfq.imageAlt: Menz RFQ Copilot analysing a synthetic technical request

rag.name: Second Brain RAG Security Lab
rag.summary: A visual lab for testing how a malicious note can influence a RAG workflow.
rag.problem: Retrieved content can contain instructions, and a valid citation does not prove an answer is grounded.
rag.solution: Reproduces attacks with synthetic notes, exposes the chain of custody and compares original and hardened behaviour.
rag.how: The lab follows retrieval, context, quarantine and validation to show where an instruction is accepted or blocked.
rag.try: Choose an attack, edit the note and compare exposed and hardened results.
rag.working: Contracts, Supabase functions, n8n workflows, security tests and two reproduced mitigations.
rag.simulated: The demo is deterministic in the browser and calls neither a model nor a private database.
rag.experimental: Owner identity through a trusted header remains a conditional risk pending signing and expiry.
rag.tech: Next.js, Supabase, n8n, OpenRouter, Python and contract tests.
rag.imageAlt: RAG security lab comparing exposed and hardened retrieval workflows

fridge.name: FridgeFlow
fridge.summary: A mobile view for deciding what food to use first without treating estimates as safety advice.
fridge.problem: A household inventory loses value when dates, prepared meals and uncertainty are mixed together.
fridge.solution: Prioritises use today, use soon, prepared and needs confirmation, with manual or Telegram input.
fridge.how: The application keeps inventory and events; the voice workflow proposes structured changes and routes uncertainty to review.
fridge.try: Explore the synthetic household and inspect items, priorities, activity and connections.
fridge.working: Responsive application, Supabase model, actions, events and a prepared Telegram integration.
fridge.simulated: The public Pages build and its screenshot use a synthetic household and require no login.
fridge.experimental: Voice interpretation and automation need configured services and credentials.
fridge.tech: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Supabase and n8n.
fridge.imageAlt: FridgeFlow showing food priorities with synthetic data

agent.name: Agent Observatory
agent.summary: An observatory for executions, conversations, commits, events and an external kill switch.
agent.problem: An agent system is difficult to evaluate when decisions and changes are not visible.
agent.solution: Brings conversation, evidence, commits and operating limits into one surface.
agent.how: Nine workflows separate start, control, Explorer, Builder, commit, observation and errors; the UI brings the trace together.
agent.try: Select a synthetic run and inspect messages, commit, blocked event and control limit.
agent.working: Two Angular applications, nine validated workflows, Supabase model and a public trace dashboard.
agent.simulated: Pages uses a synthetic trace and disables controls that require administrator access.
agent.experimental: The workflows have not yet been verified together in a production n8n runtime.
agent.tech: Angular, TypeScript, Supabase, n8n and GitHub Actions.
agent.imageAlt: Agent Observatory showing a synthetic multi-agent trace

music.name: Music School Automation
music.summary: A simple course and schedule enquiry with a structured Telegram handoff.
music.problem: A person wants to ask about lessons without understanding the internal timetable or completing a long form.
music.solution: Guides course, level, day and contact, then prepares one concise message for a human reply.
music.how: The form creates a clear payload; n8n validates it and the prepared integration notifies the administrator on Telegram.
music.try: Choose a synthetic course, complete the enquiry and inspect the exact notification preview.
music.working: Responsive application, payload validation and an inactive, importable n8n workflow.
music.simulated: The demo sends no data and only prepares a browser preview.
music.experimental: A future conversational assistant is described as architecture, not implemented.
music.tech: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, n8n and Telegram.
music.imageAlt: Music School application with synthetic courses and enquiry form
